arguments.conclusion: The record tariff revenues of 2025-2026, representing an unprecedented level of government intervention through trade policy, confirm that such intervention leads to fiscal and economic distortions.

arguments.premise_synthesis: In 2025, total tariff revenue was $288 billion, more than double the previous high of $115 billion in 2022. By January 23, 2026, the US had already brought in over $7 billion in tariff revenue, triple any prior year. Tariff revenue as a percentage of total tax revenue reached 3.72% at the end of 2025 and 7.35% in the first three months of fiscal year 2026.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The record tariff revenue figures establish that tariff policy under the current administration has dramatically increased government intervention in trade, validating the central claim that excessive intervention causes economic problems.
